identification.summary: North Korean threat actor that Microsoft named in May 2024 (formerly Storm-1789). Microsoft says it runs both financially motivated and espionage operations against software and IT, education and defense industrial base targets [S1]. Its signature tradecraft is social engineering through fake companies, fake job offers and personas on LinkedIn, Telegram and freelancing platforms. Through those channels it delivers trojanized PuTTY, malicious npm packages and a fully functional malicious tank game [S1]. It deployed its own FakePenny ransomware in April 2024 [S1]. In February 2025 it began deploying Qilin ransomware-as-a-service payloads, its first use of ransomware not built in-house [S2].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft: earliest dated activity is trojanized PuTTY delivery in early August 2023 [S1].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Moonstone Sleet (formerly Storm-1789) [S1]. Microsoft reports that early activity strongly overlapped with Diamond Sleet, including reuse of Comebacker code. The group later moved to its own infrastructure and attacks, and the two groups have since run concurrent operations [S1]. Microsoft's mapping file lists CrowdStrike's LABYRINTH CHOLLIMA as a related name [S9], but CrowdStrike's LABYRINTH CHOLLIMA is a broader, older cluster (see gaps) [S8]. Checkmarx initially attributed the group's npm packages to Jade Sleet before separating them out by code style [S3][S4]. Datadog tracks an npm cluster called Stressed Pungsan that overlaps with Moonstone Sleet [S5]. MITRE tracks the group as G1036 [S10].

attribution.sponsor: Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea). Microsoft describes Moonstone Sleet as a North Korean threat actor [S1] and later as 'a North Korean state actor' [S2].
attribution.confidence: Attribution to North Korea is Microsoft's assessment [S1][S2]. No government attribution of Moonstone Sleet by name was found in the sources gathered. Bitdefender describes Moonstone Sleet's role in the 2025 'Korean Leaks' campaign as only 'potential' involvement [S6][S7].
attribution.basis: Microsoft telemetry, code overlap with Diamond Sleet (Comebacker) and infrastructure analysis [S1]. Checkmarx found indicators linking npm packages to Moonstone Sleet [S3][S4].

objectives: Microsoft assesses dual goals: intelligence collection, such as credential and intellectual-property theft from defense and aerospace firms, and revenue generation through ransomware, possibly also remote IT-worker employment [S1]. Microsoft says the move to Qilin RaaS continues the financially motivated line of effort [S2].

sectors: Defense industrial base and aerospace, including defense technology, drone technology and aircraft parts makers [S1]
Individual software developers and job seekers [S1][S3]
Financial services, potentially, via an MSP compromise in South Korea [S6][S7]
regions: Global; Microsoft does not name specific countries [S1]
South Korea (potential link through the 2025 Korean Leaks campaign) [S6][S7]
targeting.notes: Microsoft lists aerospace and defense intrusions in December 2023, April 2024 and May 2024 [S1]. The public npm registry gives the group access to an open-ended pool of developers [S3][S4]. Microsoft has not identified a Moonstone Sleet supply-chain attack, but warns that its access to software companies would pose a high risk [S1].

capabilities.summary: Social engineering with fake companies (StarGlow Ventures, C.C. Waterfall, DeTankZone) and fake recruiters or job applicants on LinkedIn, Telegram, freelancing sites and email [S1][S2]. Trojanized PuTTY delivered with the SplitLoader multi-stage dropper [S1]. npm packages disguised as skills tests, which Checkmarx says use a 'single-package approach' that runs at install time [S1][S3][S4]. A fully playable blockchain tank game (DeTankWar/DeTankZone) that delivers the custom YouieLoad loader [S1]. LSASS credential theft with Procdump and Mimikatz [S1]. Custom FakePenny ransomware, with one $6.6M Bitcoin ransom demand [S1]. Qilin RaaS ransomware deployed at a limited number of organizations since late February 2025 [S2].

campaigns.name: Trojanized PuTTY
campaigns.summary: Microsoft reports a trojanized PuTTY delivered as a ZIP over LinkedIn, Telegram and freelancing platforms, with a four-stage SplitLoader chain.

campaigns.name: Defense-technology compromise
campaigns.summary: Microsoft reports theft of credentials and intellectual property from a defense technology company.

campaigns.name: Malicious npm packages
campaigns.summary: Checkmarx attributes npm packages published in late 2023 and early 2024 to Moonstone Sleet, based on code differences from Jade Sleet. Microsoft notes that one variant led to LSASS credential theft.

campaigns.name: StarGlow Ventures and C.C. Waterfall fake firms
campaigns.summary: Fake software and IT consulting companies emailed thousands of education and software organizations, likely to build relationships for access or revenue, according to Microsoft.

campaigns.name: DeTankWar malicious game
campaigns.summary: A blockchain-themed tank game promoted through fake game studios and investor personas delivered YouieLoad.

campaigns.name: FakePenny ransomware
campaigns.summary: Custom ransomware was deployed at a company compromised in February 2024, with a $6.6M BTC demand. Microsoft says this was the first ransomware it had seen from this actor.

campaigns.name: harthat-api / harthat-hash npm packages
campaigns.summary: Datadog reports packages published on 7 July 2024 by a cluster it calls Stressed Pungsan, which overlaps with Moonstone Sleet. The packages saw no downloads and were pulled.

campaigns.name: Qilin RaaS deployment
campaigns.summary: Microsoft says Moonstone Sleet has deployed Qilin ransomware at a limited number of organizations since late February 2025. This was its first use of a RaaS payload.

campaigns.name: Korean Leaks (potential link)
campaigns.summary: Bitdefender reports a Qilin campaign against South Korean financial firms through an MSP compromise, with 'potential' Moonstone Sleet involvement. The leaks were published in three waves, the first (10 financial-management victims) on 14 September 2025; Bitdefender's report followed on 24 November 2025. The Hacker News reports more than 1 million files and 2 TB stolen from 28 victims.

diamond.adversary: North Korean state actor per Microsoft (formerly Storm-1789), with early overlap with Diamond Sleet [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: SplitLoader, YouieLoad, FakePenny, malicious npm packages, Mimikatz and Procdump against LSASS, and Qilin RaaS [S1][S2][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Fake company websites and domains such as starglowventures[.]com, ccwaterfall[.]com and detankwar[.]com; C2 domains such as mingeloem[.]com and matrixane[.]com; and the public npm registry [S1][S3].
diamond.victim: Software, IT, education, defense and aerospace organizations and individual developers; potentially South Korean financial firms reached through an MSP [S1][S6].
diamond.socioPolitical: DPRK requirements for both foreign intelligence and hard-currency revenue, pursued by the same operators [S1][S2].
diamond.technology: Developer trust in open-source packages, freelance and recruiting platforms, and shared tools such as PuTTY; MSP remote-management trust relationships [S1][S3][S6].

gaps: Microsoft's mapping links Moonstone Sleet to LABYRINTH CHOLLIMA [S9]. CrowdStrike's LABYRINTH CHOLLIMA is an older cluster (also UNC4034/Temp.Hermit) that CrowdStrike split into three adversaries in January 2026 [S8]. Which CrowdStrike sub-cluster, if any, corresponds to Moonstone Sleet is not stated in the sources gathered. Do not import LABYRINTH CHOLLIMA or Bureau 121 facts wholesale.
No government attribution or indictment naming Moonstone Sleet was found. The DPRK organizational sponsor (for example, which RGB element) is unverified.

Moonstone Sleet's role in Korean Leaks is described only as 'potential' [S6][S7]. The Bitdefender primary report and the CrowdStrike blog could not be fetched (host unreachable); details come from search summaries and secondary coverage.
BleepingComputer's coverage of Microsoft's March 2025 Qilin statement could not be fetched. The exact publication day and the victims are unknown.
No sources from 2026 describe new Moonstone Sleet operations, so current activity is unverified.
Overlap boundaries with Datadog's Stressed Pungsan and with Diamond Sleet and Jade Sleet npm activity are not fully resolved [S1][S3][S5].
The scale and placements of Moonstone Sleet's IT-worker job seeking are undocumented [S1].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is the developer and contractor workforce: personal devices used for job hunting, npm and other package registries, and MSP management channels into DIB and aerospace suppliers [S1][S3][S6]. STEP 2: Recruiting platforms (LinkedIn, Telegram, freelance sites) and open package registries put the first contact outside DoD-controlled networks, which limits visibility before compromise [S1][S2]. STEP 3: The template is a persona and fake-company lure, then a trojanized tool, skills-test package or game, then a loader (SplitLoader or YouieLoad), then LSASS credential theft and IP theft, with ransomware optional (FakePenny or Qilin) [S1][S2]. STEP 4: The MLCOA is continued job-lure and npm-package intrusions against defense and aerospace contractors and developers to steal credentials and IP. The MDCOA is turning access at a software vendor or MSP into a supply-chain compromise or ransomware against DIB suppliers that support Air Force programs, a risk Microsoft flags [S1][S6]. Candidate indicators: Procdump run against LSASS; connections to known Moonstone Sleet domains; unsolicited job or skills tests that require running PuTTY or npm code; Defender detections such as SplitLoader, YouieLoad or PennyCrypt [S1].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: fuse Microsoft and vendor npm and package-registry reporting into the JCC2 common operational picture for DIB and aerospace partners, because the first intrusion step happens off-network [S1][S3]. (2) Authorities: the activity mixes espionage with criminal ransomware (FakePenny, Qilin), so incidents may fall under law-enforcement as well as DoD and DC3 lanes. Classify carefully and coordinate early [S1][S2]. (3) Mission assurance: treat contractor developer workstations, build pipelines and MSP connections as mission-relevant terrain; ransomware against a key supplier could degrade sustainment [S1][S6]. (4) Coordination: work with the DIB CS program and industry partners on fake-recruiter and fake-company indicators; brief personnel about job and game lures [S1].

provenance.importedSummary: Moonstone Sleet is a North Korean-linked threat actor executing both financially motivated attacks and espionage operations. The group previously overlapped significantly with another North Korean-linked entity, Lazarus Group, but has differentiated its tradecraft since 2023. Moonstone Sleet is notable for creating fake companies and personas to interact with victim entities, as well as developing unique malware such as a variant delivered via a fully functioning game.
